issues.description: Path parameters are interpolated without URL-escaping, so IDs containing '/' or reserved characters break routing or can target unintended paths.
Pagination silently treats a malformed successful response with no 'items' field as an empty result set, risking hidden data loss.
Batch creation assumes a successful response always has 'results', causing raw KeyError/TypeError instead of a typed SDK error on malformed API responses.
BatchItemResult.status and ReviewResult.verdict are not runtime-validated, so invalid enum values can enter typed models.
Transport/network exceptions from httpx are not retried or wrapped, so callers receive raw lower-level exceptions outside the documented SDK error model.
Retry-After parsing only accepts numeric seconds and ignores valid HTTP-date Retry-After headers.
Backoff cap is applied before jitter, so the actual sleep can exceed backoff_cap despite the documented cap.
Retry timing inputs are under-validated and Retry-After is uncapped, allowing negative/invalid configuration or very long server-directed sleeps.
The package claims full type hints but does not ship a py.typed marker, so downstream type checkers will not reliably treat it as typed.
Scripted mock responses bypass API-key validation, which can make tests pass for flows that would fail authentication in normal routing.
The httpx dependency has no upper bound, increasing the chance of future breaking changes in a client library surface.
